paper.title: User Search Behavior and Knowledge Effects in Hybrid Search Environment
paper.abstract: Information processing differs across cognitive levels, shaping how individuals interpret and use information. Guided by Bloom's Taxonomy, this study explores how variations in cognitive processing and domain knowledge manifest in observable search behaviors within a hybrid environment that combines a traditional search engine with an LLM-based chat interface. Prior work shows that eye-tracking data can reveal attention patterns, domain knowledge, and personality-related differences in interactive search. By integrating behavioral, physiological, and knowledge-based measures, this study characterizes how cognitive development shapes interaction strategies in interactive search environments, with implications for adaptive and personalized information retrieval systems, and education technology.
